Global, Regional, and National Burden of Myocarditis and Its Impairment, 1990-2023
abstract: Background The impact of recent trends in the burden of myocarditis has not been reported in detail. Objectives This study aims to estimate the global, regional, and national burden of myocarditis from 1990 to 2023, using data from the GBD (Global Burden of Disease, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study) 2023. Methods As part of the GBD 2023, the authors used all available administrative health facility and vital registration data to estimate myocarditis prevalence, incidence, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), mortality, and mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) for every country, stratified by age, sex, and quintiles of a Socio-demographic Index (SDI). The MIR represents the relative mortality burden compared with disease incidence at the population level. The prevalence of heart failure attributable to myocarditis was estimated using a model-based attribution approach. Results In 2023, the global age-standardized rates of prevalence, incidence, DALY, and mortality of myocarditis were 4.84 (95% uncertainty interval [UI]: 3.98-5.80), 12.46 (95% UI: 9.86-15.70), 8.41 (95% UI: 5.63-12.59) and 0.21 (95% UI: 0.14-0.29) per 100,000 population, respectively. Although global age-standardized prevalence and incidence rates remained stable from 1990 to 2023, the absolute number of incident cases increased by 54.28% from 0.67 million (95% UI: 0.52-0.85 million) to 1.04 million (95% UI: 0.83-1.32 million). Age-standardized DALYs and mortality rates decreased by 62.48% and 60.00%, respectively, over the same period. The MIR decreased across all age groups from 1990 to 2023 and remained highest among the youngest and oldest populations, with the ratio in those 75 years of age in 2023. Conclusions Although age-adjusted DALYs and mortality rates of myocarditis decreased globally from 1990 to 2023, incidence and prevalence remained stable, suggesting potential improvements in outcomes over time. However, absolute burden has grown due to population growth and aging, and important disparities persist across age groups and SDI strata. These findings highlight the need for targeted strategies to improve early diagnosis and reduce the burden of myocarditis, particularly in vulnerable populations and lower-resource settings, while being interpreted in the context of evolving diagnostic and coding practices.

title: Clinical Considerations for the Care of the Tactical Athlete With Cardiovascular Abnormalities
abstract: Aim The American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Scientific Statement, "Clinical Considerations for the Care of the Tactical Athlete With Cardiovascular Abnormalities," was written to provide guidance and education for clinicians caring for the tactical athlete (ie, firefighters, law enforcement officers, military) with cardiovascular disease or risk for cardiovascular disease, and for the organizations overseeing the care and wellness of these athletes. The considerations are shaped by the interaction between occupational demands and fit for full duty assessments, including risk discussions about how a cardiovascular event in a tactical athlete could impact teammates' well-being, community safety, and overall mission success. Methods This scientific statement is organized into 11 sections focused on cardiovascular disease processes and other topics that are relevant when considering the potential risks and benefits of performing tasks specific to the tactical athlete. Task forces, comprised of experts in tactical athlete domains, sports cardiology, and the respective topics covered, were assigned to each section, and specific "Clinical Considerations Tables" for clinicians to reference were prepared. Comprehensive literature reviews and an emphasis on tactical athlete-focused data, as available, were integral in the writing of all clinical considerations presented. The framework mirrors that of the recently published, "Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes With Cardiovascular Abnormalities: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology." Structure The specific sections in this document include: Section 1: Tactical Tasks Classification; Section 2: The Tactical Athlete Preparticipation Cardiac Evaluation; Section 3: Ethical and Legal Aspects of Tactical Clinical Management; Section 4: Genetic Cardiomyopathies; Section 5: Myocarditis and Other Acquired Cardiac Conditions; Section 6: Congenital Heart Disease; Section 7: Aortopathy, Bicuspid Aortic Valve, and Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection; Section 8: Syncope, SCA, Arrhythmias, and Devices; Section 9: Cardiac Channelopathies; Section 10: Older Tactical Athlete; Section 11: Environmental Exposures, PED/S, and Additional Cardiac Conditions and Considerations. Each section provides a summary detailing the rationale for key clinical considerations and the respective Clinical Considerations Table(s).

title: Genetic Determinants of Early Heart Failure in Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
abstract: Background Survivors of hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), the most severe form of congenital heart disease, are at high risk for heart failure (HF). HF in early life is a major contributor to mortality in this vulnerable population. However, reliable approaches to identify infants at highest risk for early HF are currently lacking. Objectives The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether ultra-rare variants in cardiomyopathy-associated genes are associated with HF risk in HLHS. Methods Neonates with HLHS were prospectively enrolled within the first 21 days of life at Duke University Health System. Children and adults with HLHS who were older than 21 days were enrolled from Duke University Health System and the University of North Carolina into an ambispective cohort. External HLHS cohorts from Nationwide Children's Hospital and Vanderbilt University Medical Center were evaluated to assess for reproducibility across institutions. Participants underwent genome sequencing, and ultra-rare variants in dilated cardiomyopathy-associated genes (minor allele frequency ≤0.01%) were evaluated. The primary outcome was HF, categorized as severe (ventricular assist device implantation, heart transplantation, or death) or medically managed (reduced systemic ventricular ejection fraction and/or HF diagnosis requiring initiation or escalation of HF therapy). Associations between variant status and HF risk were assessed using Cox regression. Results Among 35 neonates in the prospective cohort, 7 (20.0%) developed severe HF, 10 (28.6%) developed medically managed HF, and 18 (51.4%) remained HF free. The presence of a likely pathogenic/pathogenic variant was associated with a marked 9-fold increased risk of severe HF compared with genotype-negative individuals (P = 0.02). Most severe HF events occurred within the first month of life (67%). Similar associations between likely pathogenic/pathogenic variants and severe HF were observed in the Nationwide Children's Hospital and Vanderbilt University Medical Center cohorts (11- and 3-fold increased risk, respectively; all P 0.05), which consisted of individuals significantly older than the prospective cohort (P Conclusions This study provides the first prospective evidence linking dilated cardiomyopathy-associated variants to early-onset HF in HLHS. These findings suggest that genetic variation may contribute to myocardial vulnerability in HLHS, highlighting the potential for genetic screening to enable early risk stratification and guide precision medicine approaches in this high-risk population.

Physiological Left Atrial Staging and the Risk of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
abstract: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) is pervasive and an independent driver of stroke and death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Despite guideline recommendations for AF surveillance, effective risk stratification remains elusive, and the hemodynamic and functional states of the left atrium (LA) preceding AF onset remain poorly characterized. Objectives We aimed to delineate the hemodynamic and functional states of the LA in HCM, derive a novel LA staging system, and evaluate its prognostic performance for new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF). Methods This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive HCM patients with normal left ventricular systolic function from January 2007 to February 2024 at 2 academic referral centers. Patients with valvular heart disease or prior AF were excluded. Patients were categorized by combining the presence of elevated LA pressure (hemodynamic load) and LA contractile strain (intrinsic LA function): stage 1 (normal LA pressure and function), stage 2 (relative contractile augmentation for a given LA pressure), stage 3 (loss of relative contractile augmentation despite elevated LA pressure), stage 4 (elevated LA pressure with decreased LA contractile strain), and isolated LA contractile dysfunction. The primary outcome was NOAF. External validation was conducted in an independent HCM cohort. Results Of 1,856 patients screened, 705 were eligible (mean age 57.6 ± 13.0 years, 30.1% female). During a median follow-up of 7.5 years (Q1-Q3: 3.6-11.0 years), NOAF occurred in 101. The staging system was independently associated with a significant, stepwise increase in the risk of NOAF (adjusted HR: 1.83 per increment; 95% CI: 1.42-2.37; P Conclusions The proposed LA staging framework offers mechanistic insights into how the LA adapts to progressive diastolic dysfunction in HCM. It is associated with a graded risk of NOAF and may help tailor AF surveillance strategies.

abstract: Background Recent societal guidelines provide a Class I recommendation for intracoronary imaging (ICI)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for complex or left main coronary artery disease; however, recent trials have failed to show a benefit. Objectives The study aim was to re-evaluate the efficacy of ICI-guided PCI and to explore heterogeneity of results across trials. Methods PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov databases were searched through June 3, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing outcomes with ICI-guided PCI vs angiography-guided PCI in the drug-eluting stent era. Direct comparison meta-analyses, mixed treatment comparison meta-analyses, trial sequential analyses, fragility analysis, and Bayesian meta-analyses were performed. Meta-regression analysis was performed to evaluate heterogeneity using the following variables: stent length (surrogate for lesion length), stent diameter, difference in postdilatation (percentage) between the groups, publication year, and geographic location. Results A total of 28 RCTs met the inclusion criteria, comprising 24,634 patients (mean age 64.8 years; 75.9% male) with a mean follow-up of 22 months. ICI-guided PCI reduced target lesion failure (relative risk [RR]: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.61-0.85; I 2 = 61%), cardiac mortality (RR: 0.73; 0.58-0.91; I 2 = 5%), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.86; 0.75-0.97; I 2 = 0%), target vessel revascularization (RR: 0.69; 95% CI: 0.57-0.83, I 2 = 41%), stent thrombosis (RR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.40-0.76; I 2 = 0%), and all-cause mortality (RR: 0.82; 95% CI: 0.70-0.96; I 2 = 0%) compared with angiography-guided PCI. Trial sequential analysis confirmed evidence for at least a 20% reduction in all outcomes with ICI-guided PCI. The fragility index was robust, ranging from 9 to 50. The posterior probability for benefit was >99% for all outcomes. Trial differences in geography and lesion characteristics explained most of the between-trial variance (residual tau = 0). Conclusions In this updated meta-analysis of RCTs, after accounting for modifier effects from recent studies, ICI-guided PCI was associated with significantly reduced cardiovascular events compared with angiography-guided PCI. Geographic heterogeneity across trials was present mainly for target vessel revascularization, explained in large part by differences in lesion characteristics and procedural technique.

Food and Health: Nutrition for Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement
abstract: Nutrition is a foundational determinant of cardiovascular health and a central component of the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, obesity, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome. Suboptimal dietary patterns remain among the leading modifiable causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Contemporary evidence supports a shift in nutrition guidance from isolated nutrients toward whole foods and dietary patterns that emphasize overall dietary quality, food choice, and degree of processing. This American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement reviews current evidence regarding nutrition and cardiovascular health, including macronutrients, micronutrients, dietary patterns, ultra-processed foods, and emerging nutrition-based interventions. Evidence from randomized controlled trials, prospective cohort studies, and mechanistic investigations consistently supports replacing saturated fats with unsaturated fats, increasing consumption of dietary fiber and whole grains, reducing consumption of sodium and ultra-processed foods (particularly sugar-sweetened beverages and processed meats), and greater adherence to healthy dietary patterns to lower cardiovascular risk. Mediterranean, DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension), vegetarian, and other plant-rich dietary patterns demonstrate favorable effects on blood pressure, lipids, glycemic control, and body weight, and are consistently associated with lower rates of cardiovascular disease and mortality. Translation of nutrition science into clinical practice requires integration of dietary counseling, medical nutrition therapy, Food Is Medicine programs, public policy initiatives, and clinician education. Collectively, current evidence supports dietary patterns centered on minimally processed plant foods while limiting ultra-processed foods, particularly those high in refined starches, added sugars, sodium, or unhealthy fats, and emphasizing healthy sources of fats and proteins to reduce cardiovascular risk and improve population health.

Sirolimus-Coated Balloon Angioplasty for Femoropopliteal Artery Disease Without Tissue Loss
abstract: Background Whether sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty performs better than uncoated balloon angioplasty among patients with exertional symptoms due to femoropopliteal artery disease remains uncertain. Objectives This study sought to describe 1-year outcomes after sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty among participants in the SirPAD (Sirolimus-Coated Balloon for Peripheral Artery Disease) trial with femoropopliteal artery disease. Methods In this analysis of the multicenter, randomized, blinded-endpoint SirPAD trial, we evaluated outcomes for patients with femoropopliteal target lesions and without tissue loss (Rutherford category ≤4, Fontaine stage ≤III). A secondary subgroup was restricted to patients with a lower disease burden, excluding ischemic rest pain, prior major amputation, or below-the-knee revascularization. We compared the 1-year rate of: 1) target-lesion revascularization (TLR); 2) the composite of TLR and any unplanned amputation; 3) major adverse limb events; and 4) all-cause death. Results Among 597 patients, median age was 71 years, 34.7% were women, and median target-lesion length was 150 mm; 53.8% had total occlusion. After 1 year, 50 patients (17.0%) had undergone TLR in the sirolimus-coated balloon group vs 82 (27.1%) among control subjects (absolute risk difference [ARD]: -10.1%; 95% CI: -16.6 to -3.0). Any amputation or any TLR occurred in 17.7% and 27.1% of patients respectively (ARD: -9.4%; 95% CI: -16.0 to -2.7). Major adverse limb events occurred in 4.1% vs 8.9% of patients, respectively (ARD: -4.8%; 95% CI: -9.0 to -0.8). One-year all-cause death was similar (3.7% vs 5.3%). Conclusions Among patients with femoropopliteal artery disease and no tissue loss, sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty was associated with a lower 1-year rate of TLR compared with uncoated balloon angioplasty. These findings are descriptive rather than confirmatory. (Sirolimus-Coated Balloon for Peripheral Artery Disease; NCT04238546).

Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care. OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH). METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization. RESULTS: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious. CONCLUSIONS: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).

Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD. METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year. RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year. CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

title: Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement
abstract: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

title: Occupational Disparities in Cardiovascular Risk and Management in Contemporary China
abstract: Background Although occupational disparities in cardiovascular health are increasingly recognized, a comprehensive understanding of cardiovascular health across contemporary occupational contexts-particularly in rapidly transitioning economies-remains limited. Objectives This study aimed to characterize geographic and occupational patterns of cardiovascular risk, risk-factor management, and potential prevention opportunities among employed adults in contemporary China. Methods In this nationwide cross-sectional study, we analyzed 1,421,390 employees aged 20 to 65 years who underwent health examinations at 167 centers across 24 provinces in China between 2021 and 2023. Eighteen occupations were defined based on participants' employer registration and industry affiliation, and were classified into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, with the tertiary sector further subclassified into modern, public, and life services. Age- and sex-standardized prevalence of coronary heart disease (CHD) and cardiometabolic risk factors was estimated, along with age- and sex-standardized rates of treatment and control for hypertension and diabetes, and treatment for hypercholesterolemia and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) control. Ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk was calculated using the Prediction for ASCVD Risk in China model. We then assessed changes in the proportion of individuals classified as having moderate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk under simulated scenarios that set elevated blood pressure and total cholesterol to target levels and current smoking to noncurrent smoking and compared these reductions across occupations. Results The mean age of participants was 33.8 years, and 53.4% were male. Overall, the age- and sex-standardized prevalence of CHD was 1.33% (95% CI: 1.29%-1.37%) and demonstrated a pronounced north-south gradient (P Conclusions Occupational context may provide a practical framework for identifying patterns of cardiovascular risk, management gaps, and prevention opportunities among China's working population. Despite lower observed disease burden, modern occupational sectors showed suboptimal risk-factor management, whereas simulated ASCVD risk reductions varied across occupations, highlighting distinct prevention needs and opportunities across occupational contexts.

Interpreting High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin in Clinical Practice and Emerging Directions
abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have solved the problem of detecting myocardial injury and, in doing so, created the problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are now known to be common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease, and the central challenge of contemporary practice is no longer whether myocardial injury can be detected, but whether it can be correctly classified. Misclassification occurs in both directions and with real consequence: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary myocardial infarction (MI), contributing to the overdiagnosis of MI, and chronic myocardial injury, which carries a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. This narrative review argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and instead requires integrated, context-aware interpretation grounded in 4 domains: 1) the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results; 2) the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the European Society of Cardiology 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support; 3) rigorous application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis, and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification; and 4) recognition of the non-acute coronary syndrome conditions-chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome, and others-in which troponin elevation is expected rather than anomalous. We provide explicit bedside guidance for the situations that clinicians find most difficult, including suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. Finally, we review emerging understanding of troponin biology, clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin, which may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden. Until then, that burden rests with the clinician.

Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
abstract: Background Current guidelines recommend echocardiographic surveillance every 1-2 years for patients with moderate aortic stenosis (AS). Ongoing randomized trials are evaluating transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) for patients with moderate AS and at-risk features associated with rapid progression or poor outcomes. The prevalence and prognostic impact of these features in clinical practice are unknown. Objectives To determine the prevalence and prognostic impact of at-risk features in real-world clinical practice among patients with moderate AS. Methods We analyzed deidentified data from 14,859,523 patients at 48 US institutions (egnite Registry; IRB exempt). Patients with moderate or severe AS per echocardiographic assessment (ACC/AHA guidelines) identified on or after January 1 , 2022, were included. At-risk features for moderate AS (PROGRESS trial criteria) included valve-related symptoms, left ventricular ejection fraction <60%, diastolic dysfunction grade ≥2, stroke volume index <35 mL/m , atrial fibrillation, or elevated natriuretic peptide. Outcomes were 2-year mortality, hospitalization with heart failure, aortic valve replacement (AVR), and progression to severe AS (Kaplan-Meier for mortality; Aalen-Johansen with death as a competing event for the others). Results Among 53,994 patients with at least moderate AS, 35,343 (65.5%) were moderate, and 18,651 (34.5%) were severe. Among patients with moderate AS, 27,815 (78.7%) had at least 1 at-risk feature. At 2 years, the cumulative mortality for patients with moderate AS without at-risk features, moderate AS with at-risk features, and severe AS was 9.0% (95% CI, 8.1–9.9), 20.1% (95% CI, 19.5–20.7), and 23.5% (95% CI, 22.7–24.3), and hospitalization with heart failure was 21.9% (95% CI, 20.7–23.2), 44.6% (95% CI, 43.8–45.3), and 54.8% (95% CI, 53.9–55.8), respectively (p value <0.0001 for both). With follow-up censored at AVR, progression to severe AS at 2 years was similar with and without at-risk features (28.2% vs 26.3%). Conclusions In this large real-world cohort, the vast majority of patients with moderate AS had at-risk features and experienced worse clinical outcomes, with 2-fold higher risks of mortality and hospitalization with heart failure than those without at-risk features, despite similar progression to severe AS. These findings support risk-based stratification of moderate AS and investigation of strategies to reduce adverse events in patients with at-risk features.

Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial. OBJECTIVES: This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications. METHODS: The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications. RESULTS: A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%). CONCLUSIONS: A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.
